panels.title: Audit chains currently broken
panels.description: PRD E8's nightly re-walk. This is the number infra/alerts.yaml pages on, and until program/P12 it existed only as a Langfuse span -- a tracing backend nobody is woken by. 0 is the only acceptable value: a break means either a bug in the append path or somebody with more privilege than the app editing the audit trail of a regulated recordkeeping system.

panels.title: Time since the chain was last verified
panels.description: The failure the panel to the left cannot show. A breaks gauge stuck at 0 because the beat died looks exactly like a clean chain -- healthier, in fact, than a real break. Nightly at 05:00 UTC, so anything approaching 26h means the verification is not running. 'No data' means it has never run at all.

panels.title: UC3 vendor spend (INR, cumulative)
panels.description: Charged to uc3's own ledger namespace. Per-app caps arrived with program/P12: before it, one process-wide counter meant a night's batch STT could consume the headroom uc1 needed the next morning. E13 puts uc3's variable line near the top of the programme's spend, dominated by Saaras batch STT.

panels.title: Reviewer-decided precision by category
panels.description: confirmed / (confirmed + false_positive) over the latest disposition per flag. Three rules, all of them from apps/comms_surveillance/metrics.py and all easy to get quietly wrong: latest is by `seq` and never by created_at (rows written in one transaction share a timestamp); needs_more_context and escalated are a reviewer saying 'not yet' and 'not mine', so they are in neither the numerator nor the denominator; and a zero denominator is NULL, never 0.0 -- a category nobody has decided a flag in has no precision. EXCLUDES flags raised outside the dashboard window, which is on flags.created_at (when the detector fired) rather than on the decision, so a slow queue cannot smear one week's model behaviour across the next. The B6 gate is 0.80; uc3/P7 measured 0.30 over 242 flags.

targets.rawSql:
select f.category as category,
       count(*) filter (where d.disposition = 'confirmed') as confirmed,
       count(*) filter (where d.disposition = 'false_positive') as false_positive,
       count(*) filter (where d.disposition in ('confirmed','false_positive')) as decided,
       case when count(*) filter (where d.disposition in ('confirmed','false_positive')) = 0
            then null
            else count(*) filter (where d.disposition = 'confirmed')::float
                 / count(*) filter (where d.disposition in ('confirmed','false_positive'))
       end as precision
  from flags f
  left join lateral (
       select disposition from dispositions
        where flag_id = f.id order by seq desc limit 1
  ) d on true
 where f.created_at between $__timeFrom() and $__timeTo()
 group by f.category order by f.category

panels.title: Review queue by latest disposition
panels.description: How much of the queue has actually been decided. The undecided slice is the denominator the precision panel does not have: a large one means precision is measured over a small, possibly unrepresentative sample of the detector's output.

targets.rawSql:
select coalesce(d.disposition, 'undecided') as state, count(*) as flags
  from flags f
  left join lateral (
       select disposition from dispositions
        where flag_id = f.id order by seq desc limit 1
  ) d on true
 where f.created_at between $__timeFrom() and $__timeTo()
 group by 1 order by 2 desc

panels.title: Flags raised per day by category
panels.description: The detector's output rate, independent of anyone reviewing it. Read alongside precision: uc3/P7 found recall 0.986 and clean_flag_rate 0.0, so the precision problem is over-flagging WITHIN calls that contain something, not flagging calls that are clean -- a spike here without a matching confirmed count is that.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('day', f.created_at) as time, f.category as metric, count(*) as value
  from flags f
 where f.created_at between $__timeFrom() and $__timeTo()
 group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Calls refused by a spend cap
panels.description: A refusal is the cap working, not an error -- the call was stopped before the vendor was touched. A sustained stream means real work is being turned away and somebody should decide whether the cap is wrong or the caller is.

panels.title: Vendor call outcomes
panels.description: Saaras batch STT dominates uc3's critical path and its cost. A non-ok rate that stays up means the nightly sweep is not completing, which the flag-rate panel will show as a gap a day later.
